hints.text: A sum is even when the two selected numbers have the same parity.
There is one even number and three odd numbers in the set.

solution.setup: Separate the four choices into one even prime and three odd primes.
solution.reasoning: Both picks are even with probability (1/4)^2. Both are odd with probability (3/4)^2. These cases are disjoint, so the total is 1/16+9/16=10/16.
solution.sanityCheck: Same-parity picks should be more likely than different-parity picks because three of the four choices are odd.

keyInsight: Reduce the numerical condition to a small parity classification.
recognitionCues: A condition on a sum may depend only on residue classes rather than exact values.
commonMistakes: Treating the four primes as two even and two odd.
followUps: How does the answer change if selection is without replacement?

source.notes: Original variant of a publicly reported interview family associated with Jane Street, SIG.

title: Parity of Two Prime Picks
problem: Two numbers are selected independently and uniformly from {2, 3, 5, 7}. What is the probability that their sum is even?
